name: Sri Ujjaini Mahakali Matha Devasthanam
address: 3-4-30 to 40, Mahankali Street, General Bazaar, Secunderabad, Telangana - 500003
main_deity: Goddess Ujjaini Mahakali (Historic wooden idol in Padmasana posture with four hands, preserved and covered with a silver Vendi Kavacham shield)
other_deities: Goddess Sri Manikyalamma (Ancient stone idol unearthed during 1815 excavation)
description: Sri Ujjaini Mahakali Temple is one of the most prominent, revered, and historic Shaktipeeth temples in Telangana State, located in the heart of Secunderabad. Devotees believe that Goddess Ujjaini Mahakali protects the region from epidemics, diseases, and evil forces, granting health and prosperity to all worshippers.
history: In 1813, Suriti Appaiah, a military battalion soldier deployed to Ujjain, vowed to build a temple in Secunderabad if his battalion survived a deadly cholera epidemic. Upon safe return, a wooden idol was installed in July 1815. During excavation, the ancient stone idol of Sri Manikyalamma was discovered and installed alongside. In 1964, a permanent stone idol of Goddess Mahakali was consecrated.
mythology: Famed epicenter of the grand annual Lashkar Bonalu festival in Ashada month, featuring Ghatothsavam procession, Kushmanda (Gummadikaya) Bali, the oracle Rangam prophecy delivered by an unmarried woman standing on an unburnt earthen pot, and Saganamputa farewell.
sub_temples: Shivalayam (Lord Shiva Shrine within the complex)
